**`.github/workflows/_release.yml`** — the `working-directory` `workflow_dispatch` dropdown now lists short, human-readable package names:
- Top-level packages as bare names: `core`, `langchain`, `langchain_v1`, `text-splitters`, `standard-tests`, `model-profiles`

- The `default` was updated from `libs/langchain_v1` to `langchain_v1` to stay consistent with the new option values.

**`.github/scripts/test_release_options.py`** (the validation script — not under `tests/`) — added an `_expand_option()` helper that expands each short dropdown name to its full path before comparison: top-level names → `libs/<name>`, partner names → `libs/partners/<name>` (unknown names pass through unchanged so mismatches still surface). The test now expands options before diffing against the on-disk package dirs, and it passes with no missing or extra entries.

One thing worth flagging: the workflow still consumes this input as an actual filesystem path (`EFFECTIVE_WORKING_DIR`, used in `cd`/`working-directory` throughout the build/publish jobs). With short names now selected in the dropdown, the job steps would need a corresponding expansion step to `cd` into the right directory at runtime. That runtime expansion in the workflow body was outside the stated scope (dropdown + validation script only), so I left it unchanged — let me know if you'd like me to add it.
